title: God, in the High and Holy Place
description: God, in the High and Holy Place in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 80, “The Earth Full of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God, in the high and ho-ly place, Looks down up-on the spheres; Yet in His prov-i-dence and grace To ev-ery eye ap-pears.

lines: God, in the high and holy place,
Yet in His providence and grace
He bows the heavens; the mountains stand,
The forests in His strength rejoice;
As once of old, the Lord God's voice
In every stream His bounty flows,
In every breeze His Spirit blows, —
The breath of life and health.
His blessings fall in plenteous showers
That teems with foliage, fruits, and flowers,
If God hath made this world so fair,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
